transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jared Liu (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Noah Kim (Redwood Solutions); Maya Lopez (CTO - Cobalt), Ethan Park (ML Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Infra)

Summary (auto): Discussed model selection and deployment mode. Priorities: long context (32k+), multilingual accuracy, tool-calling, low p95 latency for chat assistant, security controls. Next: pricing + POC plan.

00:00 Jared Liu: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're from Redwood, I'm Jared, AE, with Priya our SE. How's it going?
00:08 Maya Lopez: Hey Jared, thanks. We're excited, this is Maya. Quick intros from our side, Ethan, Sofia.
00:15 Ethan Park: Hey. We're evaluating options for a customer-facing assistant that needs to handle docs, long conversations, and call external tooling (e.g., db lookup, internal APIs).
00:27 Priya Sharma: Great, can you give us a quick overview of the stack and the main constraints? Latency, throughput, security etc.
00:35 Ethan Park: Sure. Currently we use managed endpoints from a public provider for experiments. Production needs: p50 around 150-200ms for simple chat, p95 under 700ms ideally. Throughput is modest - ~200 concurrent users at peak, but we expect growth. Big thing is we need long context for doc ingestion - many contracts are 50-100 pages, so 32k to 64k context would be ideal. Also multi-lingual: Spanish, Portuguese, German, English.
01:05 Noah Kim: When you say 32k-64k, is that active context (full attention) or chunked retrieval + embeddings?
01:12 Ethan Park: A mix - we do embeddings + chunking for retrieval but we also want a fallback to provide the whole convo context for summarization and tool calls. So native context length matters for latency and fewer round trips.
01:28 Priya Sharma: Understood. On models we support a few open families - some 8k/16k/32k variants, and larger 64k models in ded/priv options. Are you leaning toward a hosted API or dedicated/private?
01:40 Maya Lopez: Data residency and encryption are big. Some docs are sensitive; we need KMS-managed keys and audit logs. We prefer dedicated or private, but need cost comparisons. Hosted would be easier for dev, but security is a blocker.
01:56 Jared Liu: Makes sense. We can do hosted with customer-managed KMS for some tiers, and Dedicated gives reserved capacity and better isolation. Private (VPC/on-prem) is the strongest for audit and control. We'll map tradeoffs in the doc.
02:09 Ethan Park: Another critical question: tool/function calling reliability. We need deterministic calls to internal APIs - not just hallucinations. How do you handle tool calling?
02:18 Priya Sharma: We support structured function calling and tool integrations. On the runtime side we have fallbacks and scoring - you can enforce strict type schemas and Redwood will surface the function signature; SEs can wire the call through a safe execution layer. The transcriptions sometimes say key V cache instead of KV cache, but we handle KV caching for generation speedup.
02:39 Sofia Ruiz: For private deployment, what's the operations footprint? Our infra team is small.
02:45 Priya Sharma: For Private we provide a control plane and an on-prem package. You'd manage the infra but we provide deployment templates, operator docs, and optional managed services. Dedicated is easier: we handle the infra side but you get a reserved GPU pool.
02:58 Maya Lopez: Ok, on models: which open models would you recommend for multilingual + long context? We've looked at Mistral, Llama variants, and some 3rd-party 32k models.
03:10 Priya Sharma: For multilingual, we often recommend mixture of models: one high-quality base (e.g., Llama-family 65B quantized variants or multi-lingual trained models), but for 32k/64k context you look at model variants with long-sequence position embeddings - some open models have 32k windows, fewer have 64k. Redwood also can route to model variants: for short, low-latency use hosted small models; for long-context docs use dedicated long-context models. We'll include a model matrix.
03:40 Ethan Park: Cost aside, how much does quantization affect quality for our use-case? We care about instruction-following and tool-calling accuracy.
03:48 Priya Sharma: Quantization 4-bit/8-bit can be fine for many tasks, but we recommend A/B tests for critical tool-calling flows. For tool-calling, structured outputs and strict schemas reduce risk. For very sensitive accuracy, you might keep a higher-precision variant for certain calls. Redwood Optimize will give suggestions based on workload.
04:10 Jared Liu: Competitors - do you currently compare any vendors?
04:14 Maya Lopez: We're benchmarking Anthropic and a couple of hosted providers, and open-source models on Vertex. Cost and latency are the big differences.
04:23 Priya Sharma: Good to know. For benchmarks we usually run p50/p95 token latencies and end-to-end tool-call timings. We'll propose a benchmark harness.
04:33 Ethan Park: One more: multilingual - some languages show degraded hallucination rates. Do you have evals for Spanish and Portuguese?
04:41 Priya Sharma: Yes, our evals include language-wise pass rates for common tasks. We'll share sample eval results. Also we can run your prompts through our quality harness in the POC.
04:52 Sofia Ruiz: On security: SOC2 is required, plus audit logs and SSO (SAML). Will that be available with dedicated?
04:59 Jared Liu: Yes, Dedicated and Private can be combined with enterprise SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations. We'll attach SOC2 reports and a security whitepaper.
05:12 Maya Lopez: Great. Can you explain the routing/fallback? If dedicated capacity is saturated, what happens?
05:19 Priya Sharma: We have smart routing rules - you can failover to hosted variants or lower-cost models, or queue with a graceful degrade. Policies are configurable per route. For mission-critical flows you can also keep a warm standby.
05:34 Ethan Park: Performance targets: again, p95 under 700ms for chat. For batch summarization of docs, we can tolerate higher latency.
05:42 Priya Sharma: That aligns with how customers partition workloads. Chat on low-latency models, long-document summarization on long-context models or chunked retrieval. For many customers, a hybrid approach reduces unit cost.
05:56 Jared Liu: Recap: we'll send model recommendation matrix (32k/64k variants), pricing for Hosted/Dedicated/Private, SOC2 and KMS docs, and a POC/benchmark plan. Any final questions?
06:08 Maya Lopez: No, main question is whether Redwood can provide a 64k option and an approximate cost delta.
06:14 Priya Sharma: Short answer: yes, in Dedicated/Private you can host 64k variants; cost depends on GPU class and throughput - we'll include sample unit economics.
06:25 Ethan Park: Also please include details on tool-calling reliability and how you prevent hallucinated function calls.
06:32 Priya Sharma: We'll include our runtime safety notes and examples of function schema enforcement.
06:40 Noah Kim: I'll join the infra deep-dive next week. Sofia, does Thurs 3/12 work?
06:46 Sofia Ruiz: Thurs works for me.
06:49 Jared Liu: Okay, we'll follow up with invites and the materials. Thanks everyone.
06:55 Maya Lopez: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
